etymology: Old English efen, level, equal. Webster 1828 records four heads: adjective (level, equal, balanced), verb (to make level), adverb (emphatic identity or unexpected inclusion), and the noun eve / evening. The KJV-gap this page fills is the adverb. Companion pages already treat evening and eve. Webster’s own biblical illustration of the adverb is Genesis 6:17: And behold I, even I, do bring a flood of waters on the earth.
biblical_def: Even in Scripture is not a filler word. It presses a second thing down onto the first until they stand on the same level. God will not let the flood be spoken as if someone else were doing it: behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth (Gen 6:17). Isaiah hears the same insistence in old age: even I will carry, and will deliver you (Isa 46:4). The adverb also names the unexpected inclusion. Jesus will not let love of friends count as righteousness: do not even the publicans the same? (Matt 5:46). Philippians will not let the Cross be a metaphor: the Son became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross (Phil 2:8). Paul will not let the kingdom stop at a title: He delivers it up to God, even the Father (1 Cor 15:24). The dictionary therefore keeps even from becoming a shrug. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this, and no less; this Person, and no substitute; this death, and not a softer one.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines EVEN as adjective (level, uniform, fair, balanced, opposed to odd), verb (to make level or to balance accounts), adverb (level, equality, emphatic identity, likewise, unexpected inclusion), and noun (eve / evening). His adverb illustration is Genesis 6:17.
webster_full: E'VEN, adverb e'vn. Noting a level or equality, or emphatically, a like manner or degree. As it has been done to you, even so shall it be done to others.
2. Noting, emphatically, identity of person. And behold I, even I, do bring a flood of waters on the earth. Genesis 6:17.

5. Noting the application of something to that which is less probably included in the phrase; or bringing something within a description, which is unexpected. The common people are addicted to this vice, and even the great are not free from it. The adjective, verb, and noun (eve) are separate heads in Webster; this page is the adverb.
scriptures: Genesis 6:17
And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.
Isaiah 46:4
And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
Matthew 5:46
For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?
Philippians 2:8
And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
1 Corinthians 15:24
Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.
corruption_summary: Even is corrupted when God’s even I is recast as self-talk, when the Cross is allowed to mean a milder death, and when even the publicans is turned into a class sneer instead of a verdict on cheap love.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to make Genesis 6:17 a self-help cadence. Even I in the flood is not a man pumping himself up. It is the LORD refusing a substitute. Therapeutic religion likes the adverb as intensity — own it, name it, speak it. The recovery is the Person who actually brings the water.

The second corruption is to sand the Cross. Philippians 2:8 uses even to stop the mind from stopping at death in general. It is even the death of the cross — public, cursed, particular. Inspirational talk prefers a cross as jewelry or as a symbol of trying hard. Paul will not permit the milder noun.

The third corruption is to hear Matthew 5:46 as contempt for a tax class. Jesus is not sneering at publicans as a caste. He is measuring love that only loves its own and finding it already on the street. Progressive moralism flips the verse into a politics of who is in. The adverb here is a level: if pagans already do this, it is not righteousness.
roots_summary: Old English efen, level, equal. Love that only loves its own is already what even the publicans do (Matt 5:46); it is not righteousness.
Obedient unto death, even the death of the cross (Phil 2:8) — the adverb forbids a milder Cross.

etymology: Old English ǣfre ǣlc / Middle English everich: ever + each. Webster 1828: each individual of a whole collection or aggregate number. The word includes the whole number, but each separately stated or considered. His illustration is Psalm 39:5: Every man at his best state is altogether vanity. The KJV uses it for the imagination of the heart, for every living thing, for every idle word, for every knee, and for every good gift.
biblical_def: Every in Scripture is not a slogan for inclusion. It is the whole number taken one by one, with none left out of the count and none allowed to hide in the crowd. The flood generation is diagnosed that way: every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually (Gen 6:5). Providence is that wide: the LORD satisfiest the desire of every living thing (Ps 145:16). Judgment is that particular: every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment (Matt 12:36). Worship will be that universal: every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God (Rom 14:11). Gift is that complete: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above (Jas 1:17). The dictionary therefore will not let every become a brand. It is God’s way of refusing both the anonymous mass and the boutique exception. Each one. The whole set. No remainder.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines EVERY as an adjective from Old English everich: each individual of a whole collection or aggregate number. The word includes the whole number, but each separately stated or considered. He quotes Psalm 39:5.
webster_full: EV'ERY, adjective [Old Eng. everich. It is formed from ever.] Each individual of a whole collection or aggregate number. The word includes the whole number, but each separately stated or considered.
Every man at his best state is altogether vanity. Psalms 39:5.
Webster refuses a crowd that swallows the person, and a person who slips the count. Every keeps both: the whole, and the one.
scriptures: Genesis 6:5
And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
Psalm 145:16
Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.
Matthew 12:36
But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
Romans 14:11
For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.
James 1:17
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
corruption_summary: Every is corrupted when it becomes a marketing of inclusion without repentance, when idle words are treated as harmless, and when every good gift is recast as self-generated wellness.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to make every a banner. Progressive religion loves the word as a membership slogan — every identity, every path, every truth. Scripture uses it as a count, not a brand. Genesis 6:5 is not celebrating diversity of imagination. It is total depravity taken one thought at a time. The recovery is the whole race under one diagnosis, and then one Mediator.

The second corruption is to shrink Matthew 12:36. Therapeutic talk treats speech as venting and words as tools. Jesus says every idle word goes to account. Not only the public ones. Not only the cruel ones. The adverbial force of every here is particular judgment, not a vibe of authenticity.

The third corruption is to relocate James 1:17. Wellness culture and self-help religion treat good gifts as techniques you generate. James locates every good gift and every perfect gift as coming down from the Father of lights. If it is good, it is from above. If it is from you as source, it is not the gift he named.

etymology: Middle English therefore: there + for. Webster 1828: for that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated; then consequently; then in return. His illustrations are Luke 14:20 (I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come) and Matthew 19:27 (What shall we have therefore?). The KJV uses it for the leaving of father and mother, for the expulsion from Eden, for justification’s peace, for no condemnation, and for the living sacrifice.
biblical_def: Therefore in Scripture is not a throat-clearing. It is the hinge that makes a doctrine become a life. Genesis does not treat marriage as a mood: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife (Gen 2:24) — the one-flesh union follows from how she was taken from him. Judgment has the same hinge: Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden (Gen 3:23). Paul will not leave justification as a theory: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God (Rom 5:1). Union with Christ has a matching clause against the bench: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:1). Mercy then commands a body: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice (Rom 12:1). The dictionary therefore keeps the adverb from becoming a filler between paragraphs. Where God has spoken a ground, He requires a consequence. No therefore, no obedience that knows why.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines THEREFORE as an adverb from there and for: for that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated; consequently; in return or recompense. He quotes Luke 14:20 and Matthew 19:27.
webster_full: THEREFORE, adverb ther'fore. [there and for.] 1. For that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated. I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come. Luke 14:20.
2. Consequently. He blushes; therefore he is guilty.
3. In return or recompense for this or that. What shall we have therefore? Matthew 19:27. Webster will not let the adverb float. It always points back to a ground already laid.
scriptures: Genesis 2:24
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Genesis 3:23
Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
Romans 5:1
Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
Romans 8:1
There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
Romans 12:1
I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
corruption_summary: Therefore is corrupted when doctrine is stored without obedience, when peace is claimed without justification, and when marriage’s therefore is replaced by a self-invented union.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is a church that loves Romans without the hinge. Justification is collected as a comfort and never becomes Romans 12:1. Therapeutic religion wants peace as a feeling and drops the ground. Paul’s therefore in Romans 5:1 is peace through our Lord Jesus Christ after justification by faith — not calm as a technique.

The second corruption is to claim Romans 8:1 as a slogan for people still walking after the flesh as a rule of life. The verse is for those in Christ Jesus. Antinomian talk uses no condemnation to cancel holiness. Paul’s next move is the living sacrifice. The adverb is not a permission slip. It is the gospel becoming a walk.

The third corruption is to unhook Genesis 2:24. The therefore of marriage follows from the woman taken from the man, one flesh, father and mother left. Progressive readings replace that ground with consent-as-sufficient and sex-as-identity. The verse will not travel to a union God did not make. The adverb still points at Eden, not at the age.
